messages:
olivia: Seeing a spike of 502s from the Python SDK in prod starting ~09:12 UTC. Happening after sustained traffic (~900-1.2k rps) to the embeddings endpoint. Errors look like connection pool exhaustion + timeouts.

olivia: Sample error from logs: `httpcore._exceptions.PoolTimeout` then downstream `502 Bad Gateway` from our edge. Latency jumps before errors.

support-bot: Received incident ticket #INC-2026-332. Can you paste a minimal repro + sdk/httpx versions?

sam: Which redwood-py + httpx versions are you on? Also are you creating a new AsyncClient per request or reusing one?

olivia: redwood-py 0.9.1, httpx 0.23.3. We wrap the SDK call inside a FastAPI route and we were instantiating AsyncClient inside our helper for each request (bad idea i know). Quick snippet:

olivia: ```py
async def embed(req):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
        r = await client.post(url, json=payload)
        return r.json()
```

olivia: We thought `async with` would clean up, but under high concurrency the connector seems to run out of sockets.

sam: That pattern should be fine normally, but creating/destroying many clients under high concurrency can blow through ephemeral ports and TCP TIME_WAIT. Also httpx connection pool limits default to 10 per host which can cause queueing.

derek: Can you try reusing a single AsyncClient instance and increasing httpx.Limits? e.g.:

derek: ```py
limits = httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=100, max_connections=500)
client = httpx.AsyncClient(limits=limits)
# reuse `client` across requests, call await client.aclose() on shutdown
```

olivia: Will try. Any quick mitigation that doesn't require code deploy?

sam: On the infra side we temporarily bumped upstream worker counts and increased proxy circuit limits to reduce 502s. Also suggested enabling connection reuse at the app layer.

eng-runtime: Heads up: we pushed a minor SDK patch in the next release that adds a connection-pooling guide and a debug flag that surfaces httpx pool metrics in logs. We're planning to cut 0.9.3 today.

olivia: Reused global AsyncClient with higher limits + set `trust_env=False` and connection issues dropped to almost zero in canary. No more PoolTimeouts. :tada:

support-bot: Marking incident resolved in ticket INC-2026-332, follow-up action: docs update + SDK changelog entry for connection pooling guidance.

eng-runtime: Release note: redwood-py 0.9.3 - recommends single AsyncClient per process, includes example for FastAPI and a note about uvloop/asyncio event loop compatibility. deploy-bot: rolled 0.9.3 to staging at 14:22 UTC.

olivia: Thanks all — will schedule a PR to update our internal examples to the reuse pattern and pin the SDK to >=0.9.3.
